notes.subject: other
notes.text: Traffic drives on the left; the only other left-driving Mediterranean island country is Cyprus.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Limestone rock walls are everywhere and on their own are usually enough to name the island.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Slightly hilly, dry farmland with cacti and dry shrubs; many roads are only one or two lanes wide.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Plates carry the blue EU strip on the left, but short plates are very common, unlike most of Europe.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Double yellow no-parking lines at the roadside, like the UK and Ireland.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Traditional enclosed wooden balconies, often painted in bright colours, are very common.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Mostly low-rise buildings in white to beige; limestone construction is fairly common.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: The word for street is "triq", on almost every street sign.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Latin script with unique letters Ċ Ġ Ħ Ż. Many signs are also in a widely spoken global language.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Bus stops are common and sometimes carry helpful location information.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Metal guardrails are rare on the smaller island; low stone barriers are used instead.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: All bus routes on the smaller island are numbered in the 300s.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Distinctive blue signs are found only in the capital city.
